# Introduction

This post demonstrates how R and Python can be used together in the same
Quarto document.Use the `reticulate` package to pass objects between R
and Python.

**Data source:** [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/)

# Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(reticulate)
```

# Calculate a result in R
```{r}
species_mass <- penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    mean_body_mass_g = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  species_mass
```

# Use the R object in Python

```{python}
species_mass_summary = r.species_mass
print(species_mass_summary)

mean_mass = species_mass_summary["mean_body_mass_g"].mean()
print(f"Mean body mass: {mean_mass:.2f} g")
```
# Use the python object in R
```{r}
mean_mass_from_python <- py$mean_mass

mean_mass_from_python
```
